Ara2 sir is very easy-going and one of the most humble faculty members. He teaches extremely well and practices many exercises in class related to each topic. He gives around 4 homework/ assignments, and quiz questions are usually taken from the homework. The midterm and final exam questions are of the same type as the practice problems.
Only the final exam includes some theory parts, such as a few MCQs and 2–3 proof-based questions. Students are required to answer only one proof question, and he informs the class in advance which proof will appear in the exam. He also gives clear suggestions about the exam pattern and often sets questions exactly as discussed.
The most important thing is to regularly practice the exercises done in class. He gives bonus marks to students who solve practice problems during class, although he does not announce it openly. He writes the names on a white paper at the end of the class.
attending all classes is essential if you do not want to miss out on bonus marks.

comments.label: Reply by Shafayat Osman to Jarif Mohsin's reply a year ago
comments.text:
Jarif Mohsin In my opinion, electives should be used to explore new fields of interest. Let’s say you are in your third or fourth year and you still don’t know which field of CS you want to work on or pursue in future. Electives can be a major help here. Take electives from different trails like ML or Networking or Software Engineering and see which of these fields you resonate with the most. These courses can serve as the gateway to your future field of expertise. Alternatively, you can also use electives as a means to dip your toe in a new field if you are already well-versed in an area. For example, my prime research interest is Cybersecurity and Computer Networks. But during my undergrad, I did my electives from ML and Theoretical Computer Science to learn about new things since I was well versed in CyberSec and Networking through my own self-study.
To sum up: use the electives to either see which field you want to work on or to see what other fields look like if you already have an expertise.
